structural_memory.memory: Port-state control is a separate external enforcement layer from flag-state administration and classification/statutory assurance. Structurally distinct roles include the port-state authority and inspector, flag administration, classification or other delegated organization, owner/manager, master/crew, port agent and the port-call interface.

Inspection targeting or selection is its own state before physical boarding. A vessel can be selected, prioritized or otherwise made inspection-relevant without that state itself proving any deficiency.

Port-call arrival and inspection availability form a timing state: inspection may intersect berth, cargo, pilotage or departure timing, so the control event can constrain a voyage even before a final finding exists.

Boarding and inspection scope are states rather than a single binary event. The actual scope can include different documentary, physical and operational areas, while exact procedures and jurisdiction-specific mandates remain Evidence work.

Document or certificate checking is a distinct observation channel. Presence, absence or apparent validity of documents should not be collapsed into physical condition, crew performance or ultimate legal compliance.

Physical-condition and equipment-readiness observations are distinct from paperwork checks. An inspection record can identify an observed issue without becoming a complete survey of the vessel's underlying condition.

Crew operational readiness, familiarization or safety-management execution can become an inspection concern separate from certificates and hardware. The state is an observed external-control interaction, not proof of broad competence or causation.

A finding or deficiency is a recorded inspection state with scope and timing. Deficiency existence, category, severity and legal consequence must remain separable rather than inferred from one another.

Corrective-action requirements have timing states: some observed issues may require immediate attention while others may carry later follow-up. Exact action codes, deadlines and criteria are jurisdiction-specific Evidence work.

Detention, restriction or another control action is a separate state from the underlying deficiency. The operational constraint can exist while factual, technical or legal questions about root cause remain unresolved.

Inspection findings can trigger a coordination chain among vessel/company, flag administration, class or delegated organization and port-state authority. Notification, attendance, repair planning and documentary response may progress on different clocks.

Rectification, reinspection or other verification and acceptance are distinct closure states. Repair completion does not automatically equal authority verification, and authority verification does not erase the prior inspection history.

Release or lifting of a restriction is a final control-state transition for the port call, while the historical inspection/deficiency record can remain relevant to later commercial or regulatory screening. Exact future-targeting algorithms remain deferred.

Class or statutory certificates do not structurally immunize a vessel from an independent port-state inspection; continuous/ delegated assurance and port-state enforcement must remain separate layers.

A PSC inspection record is evidence of what an inspection authority recorded within its scope and time, not automatic proof of every underlying physical fact, legal seaworthiness conclusion or causal explanation.

Detention or restriction time belongs in effective vessel availability: it can disrupt berth/departure timing, charter commitments and downstream schedule even though nominal fleet capacity is unchanged.

Point-in-time replay should distinguish inspection start, finding/notification, corrective action, verification and release known-times; later rectification must not leak backward into the earlier inspection state.
Independent inspection/survey as an external assurance mechanism overlaps the broader commercial and condition-survey structure already represented by earlier Shipping memory.
Class/statutory certificates, delegated organizations and open-item follow-up overlap the classification/statutory assurance layer recovered immediately before this pass.

reviewed_no_specific_memory: Exact deficiency codes, action codes, detention criteria, release conditions and inspection procedures are too rule- and jurisdiction-specific for blind retention.
Exact regional MOU membership, targeting formulas, flag performance lists or ranking methodology require dated authoritative Evidence.
Named-vessel inspection histories, detention events and current inspection records are deferred to claim-scoped Evidence.
Private regional PSC-support, compliance-consulting, training and inspection-service provider lineages are not recalled with enough confidence for structured retention.
negative_space: Exact port-state inspection selection and risk-scoring mechanics by period and jurisdiction.
Exact deficiency/action taxonomies and legal consequences attached to individual findings.
Historical non-English predecessor terminology and regional enforcement practices requiring source archaeology.
Named authority, vessel, flag, company or port performance histories and current-state rankings.
epistemic_boundary: Memory-only orientation/source-discovery output. It is not regulatory, safety, port-state, class, statutory, operational or legal advice and does not establish any named vessel, authority, flag, company, inspection, deficiency, detention or compliance fact.
stop_reason: The structural PSC lifecycle is recalled at useful category resolution. Further depth would become deficiency-code-, detention-criterion-, MOU-, flag-, vessel-, inspection-record-, provider- or jurisdiction-specific and therefore requires Evidence rather than more blind recall.
